questions.question: You’re at a party and your friend’s dog starts barking loudly. What would be the most appropriate response if you wanted to calm them down?
options: Don’t worry about it! It’s just a dog.
I’m sorry, I didn’t realise the dog was so noisy. Let me see if I can quiet it.
The dog is probably excited about the food on the table.
Maybe you should take the dog outside for a walk.
questions.answer: I’m sorry, I didn’t realise the dog was so noisy. Let me see if I can quiet it.

questions.question: Your colleague says, *'I think we should move the meeting to tomorrow morning.'* How would you politely respond if you disagree?
options: That’s a great idea! Let’s do it tomorrow.
I’m not sure that’s a good time—maybe we could try another day?
I agree, tomorrow is perfect—let’s book it!
I think we should stick to the original time, but I’ll check with everyone.
questions.answer: I’m not sure that’s a good time—maybe we could try another day?

questions.question: A stranger asks you for directions to the nearest supermarket. What would be the most appropriate way to respond?
options: Sorry, I don’t know. You’ll have to ask someone else.
Yes, go straight ahead and turn left at the traffic lights. It’s about five minutes away.
That’s a good question. Maybe you should look on Google Maps.
I don’t think you’ll find one near here—try another area.
questions.answer: Yes, go straight ahead and turn left at the traffic lights. It’s about five minutes away.

questions.question: Your friend says, *'I’ve been meaning to ask you—do you think we should get a dog?'* How would you respond if you’re unsure but want to encourage further discussion?
options: Of course! A dog would be amazing for us.
That’s a really good idea. I’ll think about it and get back to you.
I’m not sure, but I think it’s a fantastic suggestion—let’s talk more about it.
I don’t think dogs are right for us. Maybe a cat instead?
questions.answer: I’m not sure, but I think it’s a fantastic suggestion—let’s talk more about it.

questions.question: In a formal email to a university professor, you want to ask for advice on a research topic. What would be the most appropriate opening line?
options: Hi Professor, I hope you’re doing well! I was wondering if you could help me with my project.
Dear Professor, I’m really interested in your work and wanted to ask if you could review my paper.
Professor, could you please give me some tips on how to improve my essay?
Hi, I’m writing to ask if you have any spare time to chat about my research.
questions.answer: Dear Professor, I’m really interested in your work and wanted to ask if you could review my paper.
